 Don’t wait for the first snowfall: AAA shares winter driving safety tips
 WIVB Follow Gwyn Napier Thu, November 12, 2026 at 6:09 PM UTC Add to Preferred Sources Thu, November 12, 2026 at 6:09 PM UTC CHEEKTOWAGA, N.Y. (WIVB) -- With colder temperatures approaching, AAA is reminding drivers not to wait until the first snowfall to prepare their vehicles for winter weather.
 After a relatively mild fall, some drivers may have put routine maintenance on the back burner. But AAA says checking tires, batteries, fluid levels and windshield wipers now could help prevent problems when temperatures drop and roads become icy.
 "We had such a mild fall that a lot of people put their car maintenance on the back burner," AAA director of public relations for AAA Elizabeth Carey said. "So AAA is reminding everyone to prepare for the winter weather now before it gets bad."
 Advertisement Advertisement That preparation starts with making sure vehicles are in good working condition, including checking tires, batteries, fluid levels and windshield wipers.
 AAA also recommends keeping a winter emergency kit inside every vehicle in case drivers become stranded or experience car trouble.
 "You want to make sure you pack that winter kit now and keep it in your car all winter long," Carey said.
 The kit should include blankets, warm clothing, snacks, water and basic tools such as jumper cables. Carey also recommends bringing pet treats and other supplies for four-legged passengers traveling with their owners.
 Advertisement Advertisement Tire condition is another important part of winter preparation. Kevin Fortner, AAA's fleet operations manager, says drivers should pay close attention to tire tread before heading out on snow-covered or icy roads.
 Fortner demonstrated how drivers can use a quarter to check their tire tread, but cautioned that meeting the minimum requirements for a New York state vehicle inspection does not necessarily mean tires are ready for winter conditions.
 "You want to make sure you've got a little bit more tread than that in the event you're traveling through anything that's snow, slick, or icy," Fortner said.
 Once winter weather arrives, AAA says slowing down and allowing extra space between vehicles is essential.
 Advertisement Advertisement When asked about the biggest mistakes drivers make during winter weather, Fortner pointed to three things: "Speed. And just not being prepared and not being patient."
 He said drivers who rush or take unnecessary risks may find themselves sliding off the road or unable to stop in time at intersections and traffic signals.
 AAA also recommends having vehicle batteries tested before extreme cold sets in. Carey said battery-related calls increase during particularly cold winter mornings when drivers discover their vehicles will not start.
 If a vehicle breaks down or slides off the road in slippery conditions, Carey advises drivers to remain inside with their seatbelts fastened, and call for assistance.
 Advertisement Advertisement "The best rule of advice is to stay in your vehicle with your seatbelt on and call for help," Carey said.
 She warned that getting out of the vehicle could put drivers in danger if another vehicle also loses control on slippery roads. The exception is if deep snow blocks the vehicle's tailpipe, creating a risk of exhaust fumes entering the car.
 Drivers who encounter disabled vehicles along the roadside should also remember to slow down and, when safe, move over to give motorists and emergency responders room.
 Fortner said patience and preparation can go a long way when conditions deteriorate.
 His advice for drivers heading into the winter season is simple: "Just remember to slow down out there. Stay safe."
 Advertisement Advertisement AAA says taking the time to prepare now could help drivers avoid unexpected breakdowns and stay safer throughout the winter months.
